readings.title: Esau Sells His Birthright
readings.text: [Genesis 25:27] And the boys grew. And Ěsaw became a man knowing how to hunt, a man of the field, while Yaʽaqoḇ was a complete man, dwelling in tents. [28] And Yitsḥaq loved <dn>את</dn> Ěsaw because he ate of his game, but Riḇqah loved <dn>את</dn> Yaʽaqoḇ. [29] And Yaʽaqoḇ cooked a stew, and Ěsaw came in from the field, and he was weary. [30] And Ěsaw said to Yaʽaqoḇ, “Please let me swallow some of this red stew, for I am weary.” Therefore his name was called Eḏom. [31] And Yaʽaqoḇ said, “Sell me <dn>את</dn> your birthright today.” [32] And Ěsaw said, “Look, I am going to die, so why is this birthright to me?” [33] And Yaʽaqoḇ said, “Swear to me today.” And he swore to him, and sold <dn>את</dn> his birthright to Yaʽaqoḇ. [34] And Yaʽaqoḇ gave Ěsaw bread and stew of lentils. And he ate and drank, and rose up and went his way. Thus Ěsaw despised <dn>את</dn> his birthright.

readings.title: Isaac in Gerar
readings.text: [Genesis 26:1] And there was a famine in the land, besides the first famine that was in the days of Abraham. And Yitsḥaq went to Aḇimeleḵ king of the Philistines, in Gerar. [2] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to him and said, <dq>“Do not go down to Mitsrayim, live in the land which <dn>I</dn> say to you.</dq> [3] <dq>“Sojourn in this land. And <dn>I</dn> shall be with you and bless you, for <dn>I</dn> give <dn>את</dn> all these lands to you and your seed. And <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> the oath which I swore to Abraham your father.</dq> [4] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall increase <dn>את</dn> your seed like the stars of the heavens, and <dn>I</dn> shall give all these lands to your seed. And in your seed all the nations of the earth shall be blessed,</dq> [5] <dq>because Abraham obeyed <dn>My</dn> voice and guarded <dn>My</dn> Charge: <dn>My</dn> commands, <dn>My</dn> laws, and <dn>My</dn> Torot.”</dq> [6] And Yitsḥaq dwelt in Gerar. [7] And the men of the place asked about his wife. And he said, “She is my sister.” For he was afraid to say, “She is my wife,” thinking, “lest the men of the place should kill me for Riḇqah, because she is good-looking.” [8] And it came to be, when he had been there a long time, that Aḇimeleḵ king of the Philistines looked through a window, and saw, and there was Yitsḥaq playing with <dn>את</dn> Riḇqah his wife. [9] And Aḇimeleḵ called Yitsḥaq and said, “See, she is truly your wife! So how could you say, ‘She is my sister’?” And Yitsḥaq said to him, “Because I said, ‘Lest I die on account of her.’ ” [10] And Aḇimeleḵ said, “What is this you have done to us? One of the people might soon have lain with <dn>את</dn> your wife, and you would have brought guilt on us.” [11] And Aḇimeleḵ commanded all the people, saying, “He who touches this man or his wife shall certainly be put to death.”

readings.title: Conflict Over Wells
readings.text: [Genesis 26:12] And Yitsḥaq sowed in that land, and reaped in that year a hundredfold, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> blessed him. [13] And the man grew great and went forward until he became very great. [14] And he had possessions of flocks and possessions of herds and a great body of servants, and the Philistines envied <dn>את</dn> him. [15] And the Philistines stopped up all the wells which his father’s servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father, and they filled them with dirt. [16] And Aḇimeleḵ said to Yitsḥaq, “Go away from us, for you are much mightier than we.” [17] And Yitsḥaq went from there and pitched his tent in the wadi Gerar, and dwelt there. [18] And Yitsḥaq dug again <dn>את</dn> the wells of water which they had dug in the days of Abraham his father, for the Philistines had stopped them up after the death of Abraham. And he called them by the names which his father had called them. [19] And Yitsḥaq’s servants dug in the wadi, and found a well of running water there. [20] But the herdsmen of Gerar strove with Yitsḥaq’s herdsmen, saying, “The water is ours.” So he called the name of the well Ěseq, because they strove with him. [21] And they dug another well, and they strove over that one too. So he called its name Sitnah. [22] And he moved from there and dug another well. And they did not strive over it. So he called its name Reḥoḇoth, and said, “For now <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land.” [23] And he went up from there to Be’ĕrsheḇa. [24] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to him the same night and said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am the <dn>Elohim</dn> of your father Abraham. Do not fear, for <dn>I</dn> am with you, and shall bless you and increase <dn>את</dn> your seed for <dn>My</dn> servant Abraham’s sake.”</dq> [25] And he built an altar there, and called on the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and he pitched his tent there. And the servants of Yitsḥaq dug a well there.

readings.title: Covenant with Abimelech
readings.text: [Genesis 26:26] And Aḇimeleḵ came to him from Gerar with Aḥuzzath, one of his friends, and Piḵol the commander of his army. [27] And Yitsḥaq said to them, “Why have you come to me, seeing you hate me and have sent me away from you?” [28] And they said, “We have certainly seen that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with you. So we said, ‘Let there now be an oath between us, between you and us, and let us make a covenant with you, [29] that you do no evil to us, as we have not touched you, and as we have done only good to you, and have sent you away in peace. You are now the blessed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ” [30] And he made a feast for them, and they ate and drank. [31] And they rose early in the morning and swore an oath with one another. And Yitsḥaq sent them away, and they went from him in peace. [32] And it came to be on the same day that the servants of Yitsḥaq came and told him about the well which they had dug, and said to him, “We have found water.” [33] So he called it Shiḇʽah. Therefore the name of the city is Be’ĕrsheḇa to this day. [34] And when Ěsaw was forty years old, he took as wives <dn>את</dn> Yehuḏith the daughter of Be’ĕri the Ḥittite, and <dn>את</dn> Basemath the daughter of Elon the Ḥittite. [35] And they were a bitterness of spirit to Yitsḥaq and Riḇqah.

readings.title: Jacob Receives the Blessing
readings.text: [Genesis 27:1] And it came to be, when Yitsḥaq was old and his eyes were too dim to see, that he called <dn>את</dn> Ěsaw his older son and said to him, “My son.” And he answered him, “Here I am.” [2] And he said, “See now, I am old, I do not know the day of my death. [3] “Now then, please take your weapons, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the field and hunt game for me. [4] “And make me a savoury food, such as I love, and bring it to me to eat, that my being might bless you before I die.” [5] And Riḇqah heard when Yitsḥaq spoke to Ěsaw his son. And Ěsaw went to the field to hunt game and to bring it. [6] And Riḇqah spoke to Yaʽaqoḇ her son, saying, “See, I heard <dn>את</dn> your father speak to Ěsaw your brother, saying, [7] ‘Bring me game and make me savoury food to eat, and bless you in the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> before my death.’ [8] “And now my son, listen to my voice according to what I command you. [9] “Please go to the flock and bring me two choice young goats, and I make savoury food from them for your father, such as he loves. [10] “And you shall take it to your father to eat, so that he might bless you before his death.” [11] And Yaʽaqoḇ said to Riḇqah his mother, “See, Ěsaw my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth-skinned man. [12] “What if my father touches me? Then I shall be like a deceiver in his eyes, and shall bring a curse on myself and not a blessing.” [13] But his mother said to him, “Let your curse be on me, my son. Only listen to my voice, and go, get them for me.” [14] And he went and got them and brought them to his mother, and his mother made savoury food, such as his father loved. [15] And Riḇqah took <dn>את</dn> the best garments of her older son Ěsaw, which were with her in the house, and put them on <dn>את</dn> Yaʽaqoḇ her younger son. [16] And she put <dn>את</dn> the skins of the young goats on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck. [17] And she gave <dn>את</dn> the savoury food and <dn>את</dn> the bread, which she had prepared, into the hand of her son Yaʽaqoḇ. [18] And he went to his father and said, “My father.” And he said, “Here I am. Who are you, my son?” [19] And Yaʽaqoḇ said to his father, “I am Ěsaw your first-born; I have done just as you told me. Please arise, sit and eat of my game, so that your being might bless me.” [20] And Yitsḥaq said to his son, “How is it that you have found it so quickly, my son?” And he said, “Because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> brought it to me.” [21] And Yitsḥaq said to Yaʽaqoḇ, “Please come near, so that I feel you, my son, whether you are truly my son Ěsaw or not.” [22] And Yaʽaqoḇ went near to Yitsḥaq his father, and he felt him and said, “The voice is the voice of Yaʽaqoḇ, but the hands are the hands of Ěsaw.” [23] And he did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like his brother Ěsaw’s hands, so he blessed him. [24] And he said, “Are you truly my son Ěsaw?” And he said, “I am.” [25] And he said, “Bring it near to me, and let me eat of my son’s game, so that my being might bless you.” And he brought it near to him, and he ate. And he brought him wine, and he drank. [26] And his father Yitsḥaq said to him, “Please come near and kiss me, my son.” [27] And he came near and kissed him. And he smelled <dn>את</dn> the smell of his garments, and blessed him and said, “See, the smell of my son is like the smell of a field which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has blessed. [28] “And <dn>Elohim</dn> give you of the dew of the heavens, of the fatness of the earth, and plenty of grain and wine. [29] “Let peoples serve you, and nations bow down to you. Be master over your brothers, and let your mother’s sons bow down to you. Cursed be those cursing you, and blessed be those blessing you!” [30] And it came to be, as soon as Yitsḥaq had finished blessing <dn>את</dn> Yaʽaqoḇ, and Yaʽaqoḇ had hardly gone out from the presence of Yitsḥaq his father, that Ěsaw his brother came in from his hunting. [31] And he also had made savoury food, and brought it to his father, and said to his father, “Let my father arise and eat of his son’s game, so that your being might bless me.” [32] And his father Yitsḥaq said to him, “Who are you?” And he said, “I am your son, your first-born, Ěsaw.” [33] And Yitsḥaq trembled exceedingly, and said, “Who was it then who hunted game and brought it to me? And I ate all of it before you came, and I have blessed him. Yea, he is blessed.” [34] When Ěsaw heard <dn>את</dn> the words of his father, he cried with an exceedingly great and bitter cry, and said to his father, “Bless me, me too, O my father!” [35] And he said, “Your brother came with deceit and took your blessing.” [36] And Ěsaw said, “Was his name, then, called Yaʽaqoḇ? For he has supplanted me these two times. He took away <dn>את</dn> my birthright, and see, now he has taken away my blessing!” And he said, “Have you not reserved a blessing for me?” [37] And Yitsḥaq answered and said to Ěsaw, “See, I have made him your master, and <dn>את</dn> all his brothers I have given to him as servants. And I have sustained him with grain and wine. And what, then, shall I do for you, my son?” [38] And Ěsaw said to his father, “Have you only one blessing, my father? Bless me, me too, O my father!” And Ěsaw lifted up his voice and wept. [39] And Yitsḥaq his father answered and said to him, “See, your dwelling shall be of the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of the heavens from above. [40] “And by your sword you are to live, and serve your brother. And it shall come to be, when you become restless, that you shall break his yoke from your neck.”

readings.title: Jacob Flees to Laban
readings.text: [Genesis 27:41] And Ěsaw hated <dn>את</dn> Yaʽaqoḇ because of the blessing with which his father blessed him, and Ěsaw said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father draw near, then I shall kill <dn>את</dn> my brother Yaʽaqoḇ.” [42] And <dn>את</dn> the words of Ěsaw her older son were told to Riḇqah. And she sent and called Yaʽaqoḇ her younger son, and said to him, “See, your brother Ěsaw comforts himself concerning you, to kill you. [43] “And now, my son, listen to my voice, and rise, flee to my brother Laḇan in Ḥaran. [44] “And stay with him a few days, until your brother’s wrath turns away, [45] until your brother’s anger turns away from you, and he forgets <dn>את</dn> what you have done to him. And I shall send and bring you from there. Why should I be bereaved of you both in one day?” [46] And Riḇqah said to Yitsḥaq, “I am disgusted with my life because of the daughters of Ḥeth. If Yaʽaqoḇ takes a wife from the daughters of Ḥeth, like these who are the daughters of the land, what is my life to me?” [Genesis 28:1] And Yitsḥaq called Yaʽaqoḇ and blessed him, and commanded him, and said to him, “You do not take a wife from the daughters of Kenaʽan. [2] “Arise, go to Paddan Aram, to the house of Bethu’ĕl your mother’s father. And take a wife for yourself from there, from the daughters of Laḇan your mother’s brother. [3] “And <dn>El Shaddai</dn> bless you, and make you fruitful and increase <dn>את</dn> you, and you shall become an assembly of peoples, [4] and give <dn>את</dn> you the blessing of Abraham, to you and your seed with you, so that you possess <dn>את</dn> the land of your sojournings, which <dn>Elohim</dn> gave to Abraham.” [5] And Yitsḥaq sent <dn>את</dn> Yaʽaqoḇ away, and he went to Paddan Aram, to Laḇan the son of Bethu’ĕl the Aramean, the brother of Riḇqah, the mother of Yaʽaqoḇ and Ěsaw.
